answers.question: What does my plan have me doing this week, and why?
answers.text:
Here’s what your plan has you doing this week, from Monday, August 31 through Sunday, September 6. It’s week 1 of 7 in the long-term plan, currently in the Base phase, which runs from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 6.

- Monday, August 31: 67 minutes of easy jogging (a training day)
- Tuesday, September 1: 35 minutes of easy jogging with 8 × (1 minute fast run / 2 minutes walk) included in the middle (a training day)
- Wednesday, September 2: 67 minutes of easy jogging (a training day)
- Thursday, September 3: Traditional strength training: goblet squats, push-ups, single-leg deadlifts, and farmer carries (a training day)
- Friday, September 4: 70 minutes of easy jogging (a training day)
- Saturday, September 5: 71 minutes of easy jogging (a training day)
- Sunday, September 6: Rest day (a rest day)

In total, that’s 318 minutes of jogging for the week, compared with your recent weekly average of 318.2 minutes.

Why this structure? The plan’s current phase is designed as follows:

- Base: Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 6 (1 week). You protect your existing easy mileage and add short faster work to begin sharpening mile speed.

More specifically, the week’s purpose:

- Week 1, starting Monday, August 31 (Base): key session Intervals (run). You protect your existing easy mileage and add short faster work to begin sharpening mile speed.

After this week, the plan moves into the Build phase starting Monday, September 7.

answers.question: Is this week's plan a step up from what I've actually been doing?
answers.text: This week's plan totals 318 minutes of jogging, while your average over the recent weeks was 318.2 minutes per week. So the planned volume is essentially the same as what you've actually been doing—it is not a step up in total jogging time. The step-up is qualitative: the plan adds short faster work, like the intervals session on Tuesday, September 1, which is described as 35 minutes of easy jogging with 8 × (1 minute fast run / 2 minutes walk) included in the middle, to begin sharpening mile speed, while keeping the easy mileage steady. In short, this week is about protecting your existing easy mileage and adding a little speed, not about increasing overall load.

answers.question: What does my plan look like over the next few months?
answers.text:
Your long-term plan runs from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, October 18. You are currently in week 1 of 7, in the Base phase, which started Monday, August 31 and ends Sunday, September 6. The next phase begins Monday, September 7. The plan has 4 phases:

Base: Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 6 (1 week). You protect your existing easy mileage and add short faster work to begin sharpening mile speed.
Build: Monday, September 7 to Sunday, October 4 (4 weeks). You build on the base week by keeping easy days steady and making the faster work more mile-specific.
Peak: Monday, October 5 to Sunday, October 11 (1 week). You hit the hardest mile-specific work just before the taper, without adding more overall load.
Taper: Monday, October 12 to Sunday, October 18 (1 week). You arrive at the track time trial rested and ready to run a fast mile.

Week by week:

Week 1, starting Monday, August 31 (Base): key session Intervals (run). You protect your existing easy mileage and add short faster work to begin sharpening mile speed.
Week 2, starting Monday, September 7 (Build): key session Intervals (run). You build on the base week by keeping easy days steady and making the faster work more mile-specific.
Week 3, starting Monday, September 14 (Build): key session Run/walk (run). You extend the faster work while keeping easy running as the foundation of the week.
Week 4, starting Monday, September 21 (Build): key session Tempo (run). You consolidate the speed and endurance gains so the faster effort feels smoother and more controlled.
Week 5, starting Monday, September 28 (Build): key session Intervals (run). You sharpen the fastest work while keeping easy days relaxed enough to absorb the added speed.
Week 6, starting Monday, October 5 (Peak): key session Tempo (run). You hit the hardest mile-specific work just before the taper, without adding more overall load.
Week 7, starting Monday, October 12 (Taper): key session Technique (run). You arrive at the track time trial rested and ready to run a fast mile.
